//overrides: @grpc/grpc-js: @firebase/firestore declares `~1.9.0`, which pins the tree to
1.9.16 -- inside the vulnerable range (<=1.13.5) for GHSA-m9gg-hp2v-232j
(getAuthContext can return unauthorized certificates as authorized) and
GHSA-f596-whhp-79r4 (server handler errors leak into client status
messages). There is no forward fix: even @firebase/firestore@latest still
declares `~1.9.0`, and npm's own `audit fix --force` proposes downgrading
firebase three majors to 9.14.0, which is worse than the finding. So the
patched grpc-js is forced in here instead.
READ THIS BEFORE ADDING A FIRESTORE IMPORT. This override is safe ONLY
because nothing in this app imports `firebase/firestore`. src/lib/firebase.ts
dynamically imports `firebase/app` and `firebase/auth` and nothing else, so
grpc-js never enters the bundle (`grep -r grpc dist` is empty) and the
overridden code cannot execute. It is not a tested-compatible pairing: it
forces @firebase/firestore 4.17.1 five minors past the range Firebase
actually tested it against, and grpc-js changed internals across 1.10-1.14.
The moment anything imports `firebase/firestore`, this stops being inert and
becomes a real, load-bearing version mismatch in code that actually runs.
Whoever adds that import owns re-verifying grpc-js compatibility at that
point -- exercise the firestore paths against 1.14.x, and if they break,
drop the override and re-triage the two advisories above on their merits.
Do not inherit this override silently just because the audit is green.
Scoped to @firebase/firestore deliberately rather than written flat, so a
future unrelated grpc-js consumer is not forced along with it.
